paper.title_en: HAMCOR: inferring X-ray coronal geometry from reverberation lags with a Hamiltonian formulation and exact photon transfer in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes
paper.abstract_en: X-ray reverberation lags probe the geometry of the corona around accreting black holes, but are usually interpreted with parametric geometries such as a lamppost. We present HAMCOR, a geometry-agnostic method that infers the coronal emissivity distribution from reverberation lags. The corona is a non-negative emissivity field on a grid; the solution minimises a Hamiltonian combining a smoothness prior with lag likelihoods and the measured illumination fraction. Photon transfer is computed by exact null-geodesic integration in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, including the energy shifts of the reflected spectrum, and the model passes through the same cross-spectral estimator as the data, with dilution and an intrinsic continuum lag. Lag-frequency spectra constrain about four combinations of the emissivity; centroids are recovered within 2-6 r_g, maps only partially. In eight XMM-Newton observations of Mrk 335, 1H 0707-495, IRAS 13224-3809 and MCG-6-30-15, six reflection fractions exceed the maximum reachable around a non-spinning hole; at a=0.998 seven become reachable and require compact coronae (R_c ~ 2-3 r_g), in tension with the lags in three epochs of Mrk 335. Lag-energy spectra fitted with the energy-resolved transfer quadruple the number of constrained parameters. A lamppost allowed down to the horizon is preferred by the Akaike criterion in all cases but one, Mrk 335 in 2006 at maximal spin, where it is disfavoured only if the reflection fraction is known to better than 0.03, whereas alternative spectral models spread it by 0.1. Current data are consistent with, but do not require, an extended corona; excluding a lamppost requires a reflection fraction measured to a few per cent independently of the spectral model together with a high-coherence lag-energy spectrum. The code is publicly available.
